name: Hood River Event Site
waterType: River, mostly flat with some chop; deep close to shore
description: The most consistently cited wing foil destination in the US. The Gorge's venturi effect (desert heat inland vs. cool coastal air) makes wind reliable almost all season, and river current adds extra glide. Gusty, with real river traffic to watch for — a beginner is better served nearby at 'the Hook.'
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28), not yet confirmed firsthand — see project notes.

name: Crissy Field
waterType: Ocean chop/swell, strong tidal current, shipping traffic
windDirection: NNW-WNW, funneled through the Golden Gate
description: The Bay Area's most iconic launch, right at the Golden Gate — powerful, highly reliable summer thermal wind, but strong current and boat traffic make this an experienced-riders-only spot. Beginners should look toward Coyote Point or Berkeley instead.
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28), not yet confirmed firsthand — see project notes.

name: Waddell Creek Beach
description: A legendary NorCal windsurf/kite spot now drawing wing foilers too — real ocean swell, not flat water, plus a reef/rock bottom. Powerful and beautiful, but for experienced riders only.
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28), not yet confirmed firsthand — see project notes.

name: Mission Bay (East / Hilton Area)
windDirection: Typically onshore/westerly afternoon sea breeze (not independently confirmed for this exact spot)
description: San Diego's go-to wing foil spot and the local favorite for lessons — flat, protected bay water instead of open SoCal coast chop, which makes it one of the friendlier beginner launches on this list.
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28), not yet confirmed firsthand — wind direction inferred from regional pattern, not directly sourced.

name: Canadian Hole (Haulover Day Use Area)
waterType: Shallow, wide-open sound on one side of the highway; ocean swell on the other
windDirection: Side-shore off the sound; varies by which side of NC-12 you launch from
description: The classic Outer Banks wind-sports beach — a 30-mile-wide shallow sound gives long, forgiving, obstruction-free rides, with real ocean swell available just across the road for riders who want it. Steady wind April through November.
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28), not yet confirmed firsthand — see project notes.

name: Lowdermilk Park
waterType: Gulf water, generally flat to moderate
windDirection: S-SW, W, and NW-N all work well; E wind is offshore — avoid
description: One of the most reliable Naples-area launches — full beach amenities and a wide range of workable wind directions thanks to the beach's north-south orientation, so fewer 'skunked' days than more restricted nearby spots.
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28); Naples/Sanibel is Will's home region, so expect this entry to be replaced or confirmed firsthand soon.

name: Scenic View (Skyway Bridge North)
waterType: Flat water over a sandbar system, deep close to shore
windDirection: NE, E, and SE are best; strong N gets gusty; W wind — use Skyway Beach West instead
description: A named favorite in local wing-foil/kitefoil guides — deep water close to the beach plus a large sandbar system that creates flat pockets at low tide, with more room than the more crowded Tampa Bay launches.
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28), not yet confirmed firsthand — see project notes.

name: Bird Island Basin
windDirection: Typically SE Gulf sea breeze in summer (not independently confirmed for this exact spot)
description: One of the most historically famous wind-sports spots in the country — steady wind, warm shallow water, and almost nothing to run into. Widely regarded as a strong place to learn as well as a serious spot for experienced riders.
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28), not yet confirmed firsthand — wind direction inferred from regional pattern, not directly sourced.

name: Pere Marquette Park Beach
waterType: Lake Michigan, needs a bit of depth off the beach
description: Named directly by a local instructor as one of the Lake Michigan spots that reliably 'gets a thermal' good for wing foiling specifically. Wide, sandy, family-friendly beach with full amenities — best sessioned spring/fall to dodge summer swimmer crowds.
sourceNote: Research-sourced (2026-08-28), not yet confirmed firsthand — see project notes.

name: Kalmus Beach
waterType: Flat to choppy, some wave action near the boat channel
windDirection: Prevailing SW/SSW/S summer thermal and frontal winds
description: Widely considered the windiest spot north of Cape Hatteras on the East Coast — a longstanding windsurf/kite hub with a designated multi-sport zone setup, and real wing-foil crossover given how reliable the wind is.
